verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.8
1. Nakula’s Father
Anxiety Because of Grasping (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, I will teach you how grasping leads to anxiety, and how not grasping leads to freedom from anxiety.
Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.
And how does grasping lead to anxiety?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano rūpaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.
verses.english: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person regards form like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
verses.english: But that form of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They regard feeling …
perception …
choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.
verses.english: consciousness like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
verses.english: But that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
which gives rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That’s how grasping leads to anxiety.
And how does not grasping lead to freedom from anxiety?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati.
verses.english: It’s when a learned noble disciple regards form like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ rūpaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
verses.english: When that form of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
They regard feeling …
perception …
choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati.
verses.english: consciousness like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ viññāṇaṁ vipariṇamati aññathā hoti.
verses.english: When that consciousness of theirs decays and perishes,
it doesn’t give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That’s how not grasping leads to freedom from anxiety.”
